1099-tax-doctor: For a physician with both employment and independent-contracting income, build the proposal around the business actually generating the 1099 receipts. Request a separate line for the physician's individual return, any medical entity, payroll, and retirement-plan coordination. The service menu describes physician-specific tiers; a tier name should not substitute for checking which income streams and entities are accepted. AE's planning project should be compared with the same physician facts, rather than with a preparation-only price.
basis-cost-segregation: BASIS describes an online residential study workflow with professional review and a report for the buyer's CPA. Map the process from property questionnaire to supporting uploads to the final reviewed deliverable. Ask what happens when the intake reveals renovations or missing acquisition records. AE is a separate candidate for owner-level planning and implementation; a residential report purchase need not replace a trusted preparer. Compare the study product and the advisory project as separate purchases.
beach-life-cpa: Beach Life's nationwide page describes remote tax, bookkeeping, equity-compensation, and advisory work. A household with both a business and RSUs should specify whether the quote covers recurring reconciliations or a one-time equity event. Location alone is a poor selection criterion for virtual service. Ask the assigned professional to identify the states and entities covered. An AE planning engagement should be evaluated against the same transaction deadline and household records, with operational accounting priced separately.
bracket-partners: Bracket Partners is a tax-credit, incentive, and real estate development adviser. It is distinct from Bracket Tax Co. A developer seeking credit structuring or project capitalization may need Bracket Partners' specialty work alongside a separate owner-level tax adviser. Build two scopes: the development transaction and the owners' wider planning. Do not infer that AE's standard advisory engagement substitutes for sourcing, underwriting, financing, or closing a tax-credit transaction. Coordination between the two projects can matter more than selecting one firm for everything.
bright-hill-advisors: Bright Hill's public materials focus on real estate investors and service businesses, and describe accounting and CFO support alongside tax strategy. Compare the service company's operating records with the separately owned property's records before requesting a joint forecast. Ask whether the same professional reviews compensation, acquisitions, and cash requirements. AE's focused planning proposal may fit a defined decision while another team continues the books. Both offers need an explicit schedule for updating recommendations when business results change.
cpa-rod: CPA-ROD describes an ongoing advisory relationship for owners and investors, including business, property, and personal-tax coordination. Decide whether the immediate need is continuing access or a bounded review before a transaction. Ask for the recurring meeting calendar, escalation route, and tasks assigned to the client. A comparison with AE should use the same planning horizon, rather than equating a year-round relationship with a one-time engagement. Request separately identified filing and accounting commitments from either proposal.
compass-cpa: Compass CPA's real estate page addresses investors, developers, syndicators, and property managers. Those roles can need very different work: partnership reporting, acquisition advice, recurring books, or exit coordination. Describe your role and list each entity before comparing engagements. A sponsor should explicitly request investor-reporting responsibilities, while an individual landlord can ask for a focused owner review. Compare AE on the narrower deliverable it actually proposes; neither firm's broad service menu proves every transaction task is included.
cost-seg-atlas: Cost Seg Atlas distinguishes downloadable output from an optional licensed review and describes a completeness threshold for that review. Ask which version you are purchasing and what additional work resolves incomplete evidence. A professional signature does not itself establish that an owner can use a projected deduction. Before choosing a product, have the filing professional review the input records and reporting requirements. Compare AE's separately scoped study and advisory services with the complete workflow, including any review upgrade.
costseg-express: CostSeg Express describes an instant PDF and identifies its studies as planning documents. For a pre-closing estimate, keep projected numbers separate from the final settlement and service-date evidence. Ask who corrects the report after closing and whether the filing professional will accept the finished deliverable. AE's role can be evaluating the wider acquisition and reporting position. A fast output is useful only if the eventual tax-return records are supported; neither delivery speed nor a marketing guarantee establishes the buyer's final result.
costsegez: CostSegEZ describes instant generation with a review option. Specify whether you want preliminary information, a final report, or a reviewed report accepted by your preparer. Compare those deliverables individually before comparing price. An owner with several properties should check whether review and corrections apply to every address or only the selected order. Ask AE for a property-by-property scope if the desired work includes both study coordination and owner-level planning. Avoid interpreting automated delivery as a statement about return preparation.
costsegrx: CostSegRx's public material lists study work with CPA-ready deliverables and reporting support. Support language should be translated into a named task: explaining a report, preparing a calculation, or preparing and filing a form are different responsibilities. Request a handoff meeting with the existing preparer and reconcile the report to the owner's basis records. AE can be compared on the wider plan and separately priced implementation. Keep engineering documentation and owner-level analysis visible as two related workstreams.
costsegregation-com: CostSegregation.com describes self-guided software, a CPA invitation workflow, and a building-basis limit for its standard product. Check the current threshold on the official site; larger properties are directed to professional-service quoting. The important comparison is whether your property fits the software workflow and who approves the inputs. AE's advisory proposal should address the owner facts and reporting responsibilities separately from the software purchase. Inviting a CPA into a platform does not establish that filing is included in its price.
crescent-cpa-advisors: Crescent's accounting and advisory relationship should be evaluated around what happens between monthly reporting and a planning decision. For an owner with changing margins, request the forecast refresh date and the financial records on which it depends. Compare that operating cadence with AE's defined project milestones. If one team keeps the books and another produces the plan, assign the responsibility for notifying both when profit, payroll, or borrowing changes. The proposal should specify who reconciles the resulting assumptions before recommendations are implemented.
duffy-duffy-cost-segregation: For Duffy + Duffy, compare the engineering assignment at the property level: plans, invoices, site information, and the intended report recipient. A new-construction project with detailed cost records requires a different intake conversation from an acquired building with limited documentation. Ask which evidence will actually be reviewed and how unresolved items are communicated. AE's owner-level scope should identify the separate analysis and reporting work needed after delivery. A construction-focused study and a household planning engagement can be complementary.
duncan-carter-tax-advisory: Duncan Carter's official physician-planning page describes work for self-employed physicians. Separate W-2 employment from independent practice receipts and partnership distributions when requesting the proposal. Ask which statements must be obtained from the practice before a useful forecast can be prepared. AE should quote the same income sources and entities if it is being evaluated for the planning work. Neither physician-focused branding nor a broad advisory package eliminates the need to identify who handles each practice and personal filing.
elite-consulting-pc: An Elite Consulting comparison can begin with the owner's planned rental acquisition and the cash still needed by the operating business. Ask the adviser to show the funding sequence before discussing an estimated tax benefit. Set aside a separate line for retirement contributions and operating reserves. Compare AE's project against those same decisions. The useful deliverable is a coordinated plan with assumptions the owner can evaluate, not a list of strategies divorced from the amount and timing of available cash.
firm1040: FIRM1040 describes preparation, planning, and resolution work. An owner with an outstanding notice should separate the immediate response from forward-looking recommendations. Request the notice deadline, the representative's authority, and the expected compliance work before beginning the optional planning project. Compare AE only against the scope it agrees to undertake. A new plan does not repair an unfiled return or suspend a notice deadline; the proposals must make the sequencing and assigned professionals clear.
fox-and-company-cpas: Fox & Company's site states a seasonal closure to new clients and offers a waitlist. Confirm present availability before making a filing or planning deadline depend on onboarding. Its physician focus may fit a doctor family seeking an ongoing relationship. Compare AE for the particular business or property decision needing attention now, with acceptance and delivery timing explicitly confirmed. Outside investments should be listed separately from practice services so a physician-oriented engagement is not assumed to cover every rental or business automatically.
gavtax-advisory-services: For GavTax, make the scope follow the legal owners and reporting entities rather than treating a rental portfolio as one account. List the operating business, each property entity, and the individual owners who need a forecast. Ask how bookkeeping information reaches the person producing the planning recommendations. Compare AE's project for the same entity map and tax years. If the proposed work excludes books or an entity return, record the separate provider and additional fee before selecting the overall arrangement.
ics-tax: ICS Tax describes fixed-asset and accounting-method services alongside specialty tax projects. An owner reviewing old schedules should identify the particular ledger issue, the proposed correction, and the new property analysis as separate assignments. Ask who reconciles historic records and who determines the return implementation. AE's planning proposal should explain how specialist findings feed into the wider owner forecast. Comparing a specialty calculation with a complete planning engagement obscures the handoff; keep the technical and advisory deliverables separately priced.
investor-friendly-cpa: Investor Friendly CPA is evaluated here for the investor's actual activities rather than the general appeal of an investor-focused name. Start with a property list and the business income that must be coordinated with it. Ask which activity records are reviewed and when the combined forecast will be delivered. Compare AE using the same holdings and decisions. A property-specific recommendation is incomplete as a selection criterion if nobody is assigned to connect the recommendation with the owner's other entities and planned transactions.
msc-tax: MSC Tax's specialty-property work can intersect with other incentive projects. Request a separate evidence list, deliverable, and responsible professional for each analysis. A document collected for a property study may not answer the questions posed by a different incentive engagement. Compare AE on the owner-level review it actually offers, and decide whether a specialist remains necessary. The selection should clarify how reports reach the filing team and which assumptions need to be reconciled before the combined plan is used.
mcguire-sponsel: McGuire Sponsel describes technical specialties delivered in collaboration with CPA and real estate professionals. If your existing CPA is managing the relationship, ask whether you or that CPA contracts for the specialty project and receives the final work. Compare AE's direct advisory engagement as a different contracting arrangement. The important handoff includes assumptions, calculations, unresolved evidence, and the reporting deadline. Multiple advisers can work effectively together when the engagement identifies the coordinator rather than assuming the specialist replaces the whole tax team.
my-cost-segregation: My Cost Segregation describes several study tiers with different review and support terms. Identify the property value and complexity before comparing its published product options. Ask which tier handles exceptions, who signs the report, and what conditions govern support. AE should quote study work separately from broader advice. A lower-priced self-service option and a professionally reviewed project are different purchases; the right comparison includes the client's input work, the preparer's acceptance, and the extra help needed after the initial delivery.
pwc: PwC's tax practice spans numerous business and specialist functions. A private-company owner should request the specific private-company or owner team rather than comparing a national service catalogue with one AE engagement. Name the company project, personal planning decision, and any international or transaction matter in separate scopes. AE may fit the focused owner review while specialist company work remains elsewhere. Compare the people assigned and the coordination obligations; organizational scale does not establish the content or price of an individual proposal.
ey: EY's private-tax materials address private clients and businesses. A family enterprise may have company, trust, and individual work performed by different specialists. Ask for an entity-and-team map showing who incorporates company findings into the household plan. Compare AE for the owner project it can actually scope, while keeping any specialized trust or cross-border assignment explicit. A single relationship label should not obscure separate deliverables, reporting deadlines, or the additional professionals required for the wider engagement.
rsm: RSM positions its broad practice around middle-market organizations. A company owner comparing it with AE should separate recurring corporate work from the owner's personal planning decision. Prepare the company's entity chart and then identify the owner returns and property holdings that need a separate forecast. Request a responsible professional for each stream. The smaller focused proposal can be compared on its own deliverables, while a broader corporate engagement may include work beyond the owner's immediate planning objective.
baker-tilly: Baker Tilly's tax menu includes compliance, planning, and specialty services for companies and individuals. An owner evaluating a one-time review should request that project as a separately identifiable scope even if a wider company relationship is proposed. Ask how specialist recommendations become implementation instructions and which ongoing work is mandatory. Compare AE on the same decision timetable and entities. A proposal with more service lines is not necessarily a comparable purchase until the owner-specific deliverables and total commitments are itemized.
bdo: BDO describes an integrated approach to a business's total tax position. Map the jurisdictions and company decisions requiring that broader work before comparing it with a focused AE project. An owner may need federal and state company analysis plus a separate personal forecast. Ask who brings those findings together and what information each team requires. Compare the written outputs and implementation obligations for the same facts. Neither the breadth of the service menu nor the initial advisory fee alone shows the complete engagement cost.
grant-thornton: Grant Thornton's business-tax materials describe corporate, partnership, international, and other specialist work. A company engagement should state whether advice to individual owners is included. Request a delivery calendar for company calculations and the personal planning decisions that depend on them. AE can be evaluated for the defined owner work without implying it replaces every corporate specialty. Compare how the two proposals handle dependencies and who resolves inconsistent assumptions before instructions reach the preparer or transaction team.
cbiz: CBIZ's public tax offering covers business, family-wealth, controversy, and transaction service lines. Build a priority list before requesting a bundled proposal: an immediate company issue, an owner-level decision, and optional later projects. Ask for the coordinator and fees for each selected workstream. Compare AE's focused planning project against the part of that list it agrees to handle. The objective is a workable division of responsibility, with necessary specialties retained and optional projects kept visible rather than assumed essential.
forvis-mazars: Forvis Mazars describes tax compliance and consulting across multiple disciplines. Distinguish recurring filing obligations from a specialist assignment and from the owners' personal review. Ask which team delivers each result and when another team needs that result to proceed. Compare AE's scoped advisory milestones with the equivalent owner-facing work. If the company also needs international, state, or other specialist help, keep it explicit in the overall plan and fee schedule rather than assuming a personal planning engagement covers it.
cost-segregation-guys: Cost Segregation Guys describes virtual or in-person study options and a report with a fixed-asset schedule for the client’s CPA. Its resource menu also includes Form 3115 information. Ask which reporting tasks are actually contracted, instead of treating a resource link as either proof of inclusion or proof of exclusion. For a property owner retaining a preparer, make report acceptance and correction support explicit. Compare AE on the separately scoped owner analysis and implementation; the engineering project and wider tax engagement need different deliverables.
maven-cost-segregation: Maven’s public service menu includes detailed engineering studies, Form 3115, and R&D tax credits. It should not be described as offering only a study or as lacking Form 3115 services. Ask which technical project fits the property and which professional coordinates the report with the existing return preparer. AE’s wider owner advisory can be evaluated separately. An owner with older depreciation schedules should request a documented reconciliation and reporting assignment, rather than infer the full filing scope from either provider’s service menu.
